{{nihongo|'''Takachiniimasu Shrine'''|高知坐神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Tosa Province]].

'''Takachiniimasu Shrine''' (たかちにますじんじゃ / たかちにいますじんじゃ, also written Takachiza Shrine) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} located in Hirata-chō Tonai, {{ill|Sukumo, Kōchi|Q655258|qid=Q655258}}, {{ill|Kōchi Prefecture|Q134093|qid=Q134093}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}}, and under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Q712534|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|lt=former ranking system}} it was classified as a {{ill|Gō-sha|Q134917316|qid=Q134917316}}.

=== Enshrined deities ===
The shrine enshrines the following three deities{{Sfn|Takachiniimasu Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1987}}.
* Principal deity: {{ill|Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi|Q8009611|qid=Q8009611|lt=Tomihayayae Kotoshironushi-no-Kami}}
* Right auxiliary shrine: {{ill|Ōkuninushi|Q276944|qid=Q276944|lt=Ōkuninushi-no-Mikoto}}
* Left auxiliary shrine: {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|Q272993|qid=Q272993|lt=Susanoo-no-Mikoto}}
In the ''{{ill|Engishiki|Q1342448|qid=Q1342448}}'' {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}} compiled in {{ill|Enchō|Q1327274|qid=Q1327274}} 5 ({{ill|927|Q30470|qid=Q30470}}), it is listed simply as “Takachiniimasu Shrine (the shrine of the deity enshrined at Takachi),” without specifying the enshrined deities. The name “{{Ruby|Takachi|たかち}}” is an ancient toponym unrelated to the present-day place name of Kōchi City (which developed during the {{ill|Edo period|ar|فترة إيدو|ast|Periodu Edo|az|Edo dövrü|bcl|Panahon nin Edo|be|Перыяд Эда|bg|Едо (период)|bn|এদো যুগ|bo|ཨེ་དོའི་དུས་སྐབས།|br|Marevezh Edo|ca|Període Edo|ckb|سەردەمی ئێدۆ|cs|Období Edo|cv|Эдо тапхăрĕ|da|Edo-perioden|de|Edo-Zeit|eo|Epoko de Edo|es|Período Edo|et|Edo ajastu|eu|Edo aroa|fa|دوره ادو|fi|Edo-kausi|fr|Époque d'Edo|gl|Período Edo|he|תקופת אדו|hi|एदो अवधी|hr|Edo (razdoblje)|hu|Edo-kor|id|Zaman Edo|is|Jedótímabilið|it|Periodo Edo|ja|江戸時代|jv|Jaman Édo|ko|에도 시대|lt|Edo laikotarpis|lv|Edo periods|mk|Едо (период)|mn|Эдогийн эрин|ms|Zaman Edo|nl|Edoperiode|nn|Edotida|oc|Periòde Edo|pl|Edo (okres)|pt|Período Edo|ro|Perioada Edo|ru|Период Эдо|simple|Edo period|sk|Obdobie Edo|sl|Obdobje Edo|sq|Periudha Edo|sr|Едо период|su|Période Edo|sv|Edoperioden|th|ยุคเอโดะ|tl|Panahong Edo|tok|tenpo pi kulupu lawa Eto|tr|Edo Dönemi|uk|Період Едо|ur|ایڈو دور|uz|Edo davri|vi|Thời kỳ Edo|war|Panahon Edo|wuu|江戶時代|zh|江户时代|zh_min_nan|Edo sî-tāi|zh_yue|江戶時代|qid=Q184963}} through the changes Kawauchi → Taka-chi → Kōchi<ref>“Kōchi Castle,” ''Nihon Rekishi Chimei Taikei 40: Place Names of Kōchi Prefecture'', Heibonsha, 1983.</ref>). In historical sources it also appears as “Takaji” or “Takamochi”{{Sfn|Takachiniimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1983}}. Its origin is unclear, but ''Tosa no Kuni Shikishakō'' points out a phonetic correspondence between “Takachi” and “Takaichi” (in {{ill|Yamato Province|Q907495|qid=Q907495}} {{ill|Takaichi District, Nara|Q1117901|qid=Q1117901}} there is {{ill|Kawamata Shrine (Q11553360)|Q11553360|qid=Q11553360|lt=Kamo Kotoshironushi Shrine}}){{Sfn|Takachiniimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1983}}.

According to ''Tosa no Kuni Shikishakō'', the {{ill|Shintai|de|Shintai|el|Σίνταϊ|es|Shintai|fa|شین‌تای|fi|Shintai|fr|Shintai|hr|Shintai|id|Shintai|ja|神体|jv|Shintai|ko|신체 (신토)|mk|Шинтаи|pl|Go-shintai|pt|Shintai|ru|Синтай (синтоизм)|simple|Shintai|sr|Шинтаи|tr|Shintai|uk|Сінтай (синто)|zh|神體|qid=Q327532}} of the principal deity is a blue-black jade stone; that of the left auxiliary deity is a blue stone; and that of the right auxiliary deity is a wooden statue{{Sfn|Takachiniimasu Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1987}}.

=== History ===
The date of founding is unknown{{Sfn|Takachiniimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1983}}. Nearby stood one of Kōchi Prefecture’s representative tumuli, the {{ill|Hirata Sogayama Kofun|Q22120134|qid=Q22120134}} (now lost), and a theory has been proposed that this kofun and the shrine together formed the tomb and ritual site of the {{ill|Hata no Kuni no Miyatsuko|Q21654186|qid=Q21654186}}{{Sfn|Takachiniimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1983}}. The ''{{ill|Kujiki|Q2716751|qid=Q2716751}}'' “{{ill|Kokuzo Hongi|Q133833194|qid=Q133833194}}” records that during the reign of the 10th emperor {{ill|Emperor Sujin|Q333530|qid=Q333530}}, Amenokara-sumi-no-Mikoto was appointed Hata no Kuni no Miyatsuko, leading to a theory that the shrine was founded around this time, though details are unclear{{Sfn|Takachiniimasu Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1987}}. Ritual remains have been identified within the precincts, and artifacts such as {{ill|Haji pottery|Q5639938|qid=Q5639938}}, {{ill|Sue pottery|ar|فخار سوي|de|Sue-Keramik|es|Cerámica Sue|fr|Poterie Sue|ja|須恵器|pt|Cerâmica Sue|qid=Q7634351}}, and jars from the {{ill|Heian period|Q193292|qid=Q193292}} have been excavated, as well as a chipped stone axe from the late {{ill|Jōmon period|Q52824|qid=Q52824}}{{Sfn|Takachiniimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1983}}{{Sfn|Takachiniimasu Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1987}}.

In the ''{{ill|Engishiki|Q1342448|qid=Q1342448}}'' {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}} compiled in {{ill|Enchō|Q1327274|qid=Q1327274}} 5 ({{ill|927|Q30470|qid=Q30470}}), the shrine is listed in {{ill|Tosa Province|Q857330|qid=Q857330}} {{ill|Hata District, Kōchi|Q1132241|qid=Q1132241}} as “Takachiniimasu Shrine” and ranked as a {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}}{{Sfn|Takachiniimasu Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1987}}. Among the place names appearing in the ''Wamyōshō'', the present location is identified with Hirata-gō (also written Makita-gō in variant texts) of Hata District{{Sfn|Takachiniimasu Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1987}}.

During the {{ill|Middle Ages|Q12554|qid=Q12554}}, there was a repair of the shrine buildings in {{ill|Genkyū|Q1194276|qid=Q1194276}} 2 ({{ill|1205|Q5229|qid=Q5229}}), and Chōfuku-ji served as its {{ill|Bettō-ji|Q11396755|qid=Q11396755}}{{Sfn|Takachiniimasu Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1987}}. An inscription on a waniguchi bell dated {{ill|Ōei|Q1193078|qid=Q1193078}} 6 ({{ill|1399|Q6422|qid=Q6422}}) cited in ''Nanroshi'' reads “Takachi no Daimyōjin,” while a ridge tag from {{ill|Tenbun|Q1192853|qid=Q1192853}} 13 ({{ill|1544|Q6525|qid=Q6525}}) reads “Takamochisha Daimyōjin,” recording construction carried out by {{ill|Fusamoto Ichijō|Q11352818|qid=Q11352818}}, the fourth head of the {{ill|Tosa Ichijō clan|Q11423000|qid=Q11423000}}{{Sfn|Takachiniimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1983}}{{Sfn|Takachiniimasu Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1987}}. A land survey register from {{ill|Tenshō (Momoyama period)|Q1145058|qid=Q1145058}} 17 ({{ill|1589|Q6759|qid=Q6759}}) refers to “Takamochi Shrine” and records the existence of a shrine floor, treasure hall, dance hall, and side hall{{Sfn|Takachiniimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1983}}{{Sfn|Takachiniimasu Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1987}}.

It is a three-bay {{ill|Nagare-zukuri|Q210684|qid=Q210684}} structure with a cypress-bark roof. The interior is divided into an inner and outer sanctuary. Some carvings—such as elephant-nose brackets, frog-leg struts, and decorative supports—date from an early Edo reconstruction. The building is designated a Protected Tangible Cultural Property of Kōchi Prefecture and is currently enshrined within a protective enclosure{{Sfn|Takachiniimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1983}}<ref name="Kōchi Prefecture Main Hall"/><ref name="Sukumo City Main Hall"/>{{Sfn|Cultural Properties of Sukumo City (Sukumo City History)}}.

The {{ill|Quercus gilva|ca|Quercus gilva|ceb|Quercus gilva|fr|Quercus gilva|ja|イチイガシ|ka|Quercus gilva|ko|개가시나무|sv|Quercus gilva|uk|Quercus gilva|vi|Quercus gilva|war|Quercus gilva|zh|赤皮青冈|qid=Q3414213}} (Castanopsis cuspidata) in front of the shrine is the largest tree in the shrine grove, measuring 29.0 meters in height and estimated to be 400 years old. It is designated a Natural Monument of Sukumo City{{Sfn|Cultural Properties of Sukumo City (Sukumo City History)}}<ref>On-site explanatory sign.</ref>.

File:Takachiniimasu-jinja, ichiigashi.jpg|Ichiigashi (Sukumo City–designated Natural Monument)
</gallery>

=== Cultural properties ===
=== Kōchi Prefecture–designated cultural properties ===
* Protected Tangible Cultural Property
** Main hall (structure) – Edo period; rebuilt in Meiwa 5 (1768). Designated on February 15, 1955 (Shōwa 30)<ref name="Kōchi Prefecture Main Hall">[http://www.kochinet.ed.jp/bunkazai/details/110-2/110-2-07.htm Takachiza Shrine Main Hall] (Kōchi Prefecture website).</ref><ref name="Sukumo City Main Hall">[http://www.city.sukumo.kochi.jp/sbc/history/cultural/p002.html Takachiniimasu Shrine Main Hall] (Sukumo City website).</ref>{{Sfn|Cultural Properties of Sukumo City (Sukumo City History)}}.

=== Sukumo City–designated cultural properties ===
* Protected Tangible Cultural Property
** Half-bodied lion statues – Works from the {{ill|Kamakura period|Q236205|qid=Q236205}}. Two Karajishi statues made of {{ill|Chamaecyparis obtusa|Q917187|qid=Q917187}} wood, each 32.5 cm tall; both lack half of the body. Designated on July 24, 1963 (Shōwa 38){{Sfn|Cultural Properties of Sukumo City (Sukumo City History)}}.
* Natural Monument
** Hirata no Ichiigashi – Designated on July 24, 1963 (Shōwa 38){{Sfn|Cultural Properties of Sukumo City (Sukumo City History)}}.
